name: Enteric Fever (Typhoid)

pathogens.why: The clinical syndrome of prolonged stepladder fever with relative bradycardia and hepatosplenomegaly in an endemic region is classically caused by S. Typhi, with S. Paratyphi producing a similar but generally milder illness.

investigations.why: Gold standard for diagnosis and the only reliable way to confirm S. Typhi/Paratyphi and obtain susceptibility data.
Typically shows leukopenia or normal counts in enteric fever, supporting the diagnosis and distinguishing from other causes of prolonged fever.
Mild transaminitis is common and helps support the diagnosis.
May identify the organism, particularly useful for detecting chronic carriers.

reasonSource: ()=>"Stepladder fever pattern with relative bradycardia, hepatosplenomegaly, and abdominal symptoms in an endemic area is highly suggestive of enteric fever. Given the risk of complications (intestinal perforation, encephalopathy) if untreated, empiric antibiotics covering Salmonella Typhi/Paratyphi are warranted pending blood culture confirmation."
